diagnostic_evidence.quote: since $S$ is a nonsingular diagonal real matrix, $B_{S;i}$ is diagonally positive definite,

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma uses B_{S;i}^{-1/2}, and the theorem's proof asserts B_{S;i} is positive definite. But if A has a zero row j with p_{ij}>0 and every draw with τ_i=j selects only zero rows (e.g. q=1 and a zero row is sampled with positive probability), then the maximum defining β^S_{i,j} is 0. Hence B_{S;i} has a zero diagonal entry, B_{S;i}^{-1/2} is undefined, and the matrix D in Theorem convRBSK is not well-defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume A has no zero rows, or define/handle the zero-row entries separately (they do not affect r ∈ range(A)); then B_{S;i} is positive on the relevant subspace and D remains well-defined.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence-rate bounds in Theorem convRBSK and all results using its D matrix are not well-defined for matrices with zero rows sampled in this way.
issues.title: B_{S;i} can be singular when zero rows are sampled
issues.why_classification: This is a degenerate zero-row boundary case with a local fix that does not change the main method or rate guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let the columns of matrices  $V_{\tau}\in\reals^{n\times d_{\tau}}$ and $W_{\tau}\in\reals^{n\times (d-d_{\tau})}$ be the orthonormal bases of the subspaces $\range(A_{\tau}^{\T})$ and $\mathcal{W}_{\tau}$, respectively.

issues.failure_explanation: If d_τ = d, then W_τ has n×(d-d_τ)=n×0 columns. The matrix W_τ^T A^T D^T D A W_τ is 0×0, so λ_min is not defined. The theorem still minimizes this quantity over all τ and uses it for k>0, so the rate bound is ill-defined in this full-block-rank case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Handle d_τ=d separately (the error is zero after such a projection) or define ξ_τ=1 for full-rank blocks and exclude them from the minimum where appropriate.
issues.overall_effect: The k>0 convergence-rate constants in Theorem convRBSK and its corollaries are undefined when a sampled block spans the entire row space, even though the algorithm may then converge exactly in one step.
issues.title: ξ is undefined when a sampled block spans the full row space
issues.why_classification: This is a boundary case with a local fix that preserves the convergence conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we denote by $G_{\tau}$ the batch-sampling matrix including the rows of a matrix $G\in\reals^{m\times n}$ indexed by $\tau$

issues.failure_explanation: In a row paving with blocks of size less than q, a draw τ may repeat indices to pad the batch. For example, Example row paving uses τ=(1,1) for the effective set {1}. Then A_τ contains two copies of row 1, so ||S_τ A_τ||_2^2 = 2||S_1 A_1||_2^2, not ||S_{T_1} A_{T_1}||_2^2. Thus the maximum over draws with τ_i=j is not the unique-block norm. The theorem's B_S and the remark's β^S formula are too small, so the claimed inequality D^2 ⪰ S^T B_S^{-1} \hat P S can fail for rows in padded blocks.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace B_S and β^S by the actual maxima over draws including repetitions, e.g. B_t = max_{τ with effective set T_t} ||S_τ A_τ||_2^2, and update the proof and remarks accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The specialized row-paving bound in Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave and the β^S formulas in Remark remark:relaxOne are invalid for variable-size row pavings with repeated padding indices; numerical comparisons using this bound may be optimistic.
issues.title: Repeated row indices are ignored in row-paving B_S and β^S formulas
issues.why_classification: The specialized theorem's bound is invalid for an advertised row-paving regime, but a contained correction using the actual draw norms preserves a comparable intermediate bound.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the mean squared error satisfies

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem states a deterministic expectation bound 'with probability at least 1-δ', which is ill-posed. The proof derives a high-probability inequality for sample averages (thm4Eq8), then takes expectation, which does not preserve the bound without an additional δ-probability failure term and does not identify the sample average with the population expectation. Moreover, Lemma 5 is applied to products ξ_j ||e_j||_2^2 while the assumed covariance condition is on ξ and ||e||_2, not on ||e||_2^2; the required covariance implication is not established. The sample-size condition also depends on S although the conclusion minimizes over S.

failure_location.quote: Taking expectation on both sides of (\ref{thm4Eq8}) leads to the sharper estimate (\ref{thm4Eq2}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must state a well-defined probabilistic guarantee (e.g. on a sample-average error) or add a population covariance condition and rederive a deterministic expectation bound without taking expectation of a high-probability inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The sharper concentration-based convergence-rate bound in Theorem convRBSK_sharper is not supported; its advertised probabilistic guarantee and numerical comparisons using it are unreliable.
issues.title: Theorem convRBSK_sharper's probabilistic expectation bound is not established
issues.why_classification: The central sharper convergence guarantee is not established and the proof's probabilistic logic is fundamentally flawed; repairing it would require a new argument or changed assumptions and guarantee type.
